name: Aboriginal Dreamings Gallery
reason: Commercial Aboriginal art gallery and shop; a retail business, though listed by VisitCanberra and Wikivoyage.

name: Brindabella Hills Winery
reason: One cellar door among many; Hall wineries are named as a group, not singled out as a destination in its own right (run rule).

name: Canberra Railway Museum
reason: Museum with historic locomotives named by Wikivoyage and VisitCanberra; open to the public for a visit of an hour or more.

name: Captain James Cook Memorial
reason: Lake landmark (water jet and globe) with its own listing on two VisitCanberra pages and Wikivoyage; a distinct lakeside stop at Regatta Point.

name: Fairbairn Golf Club
reason: A golf club, not a visitor place (run rule).

name: High Court of Australia
reason: National institution open to visitors on weekdays, named by Wikivoyage and VisitCanberra (run rule on national institutions).

name: Lake Tuggeranong
reason: Wikivoyage Tuggeranong names the lake with a walk and cycle path around its edge; a district lake visitors use for a stroll, two counted sources.

name: Mulligans Flat Woodland Sanctuary
reason: Wildlife sanctuary with trails, quolls and a twilight tour named by VisitCanberra, Wikivoyage and the ACT parks page.

name: National Gallery of Australia
reason: National institution with the Blue Poles and the Aboriginal art collection; four counted sources.

name: Parliamentary Triangle
reason: A precinct whose institutions are separate spots; Wikivoyage names it as the district to walk, but as a spot it overlaps those. Case for: two counted sources and a Wikipedia tourist-attraction category. Case against: an area, not a place with one thing to see.
